DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is PythonObjectDriver; this is a decorated direct Driver over the override entry control_tools.pb_controller:PBController, the controller ROSWorld(sim_only=True) builds (plan_tools/ros_world.py:15-38), so the e-stop below can be declared. SCOPE: both arms through cap.motion.joint_position.v1 (command_arm for the left arm, then the right, with the upstream executor's timeout=1.0, control_tools/execution.py:94; reached compares the read-back with the command within follow_trajectory's 5e-3*pi rad goal tolerance, pb_controller.py:104), the torso lift joint as a written and read-back state field, and the 14 arm angles as state. Bounds: the PR2 safety-controller soft limits of control_tools/common.py:14, 19-23, 26-30; the four roll joints are continuous in the URDF the world loads (pr2.urdf:2148, 2304, 3143, 3299) and carry no bound. Not covered: grippers, head, attachments, perception, planning, plan execution, gravity. STOP: R1, simulated. ROSWorld switches real-time simulation off (ros_world.py:27); with execute_motor_control false (pb_controller.py:23) a command sets joint positions kinematically and steps nothing (pb_controller.py:145-146). The e-stop, after the runtime latched, sets execute_motor_control false and reads it back, and every command refuses to run while it is set, because with it command_torso also calls control_joint (pb_controller.py:77-78) and the motor-control loops step the physics inside the call and check for no stop (83-101, 124-143). Each command (the arm move and the torso write) checks for cancellation and makes its kinematic set under a lock the e-stop also takes, so no set happens after the e-stop returns. So after the latch nothing this endpoint calls advances the simulated PR2. The stop covers this endpoint's calls only: any other holder of the same ROSWorld or PBController in the process can still set the flag or step the world (the upstream's plan runner sets execute_motor_control and executes a plan, plan_tools/run_simulation.py:77-81), so a backend that builds the world must keep it private to the endpoint. FAKE-ONLY: the package declares only the fake backend (an in-memory PBController stand-in, F0; its start pose is placeholder data). Building the real world needs pybullet, the ss-pybullet submodule's pybullet_tools (outside the pinned tree) and the PR2 model files; no sim backend is declared because a decorated driver has one fidelity contract for all backends, and this one describes the fake. A live backend would also have to isolate stdout: follow_trajectory prints after every command (pb_controller.py:147-148). Licence GPL-3.0; the card does not require a publication review.
